scope: Tiny paired local contracts;root-owned runtime qualification is separate.

cases.title: Construct a predicate without collapsing it to a driver Boolean
cases.input_contract: Implement aboveTen/above_ten returning a Spark Column for amount_cents>10. Do not collect values or return a Python/Scala scalar Boolean.
cases.expected: Passing the predicate to raw.filter retains IDs 2 and 4. In Python, bool(predicate) raises ValueError rather than choosing one row's truth value.
cases.verification: Assert the exact filtered IDs and, in the PySpark reference, catch the scalar-Boolean conversion failure.

cases.title: Apply the predicate and preserve event identity
cases.input_contract: Return the ordered event IDs selected by aboveTen from this tiny fixture. Preserve both equal-valued 20-cent events and leave raw unchanged.
cases.expected: The result is[2,4], and raw still contains IDs[1,2,3,4]. Projecting amount and calling distinct is not an acceptable implementation.
cases.verification: Compare the selected IDs with literals and independently check all four raw IDs.

cases.title: Select missingness explicitly
cases.input_contract: Return ordered IDs whose amount_cents is SQL NULL. Do not compare the Column to JVM null/Python None using driver identity logic, and do not treat zero as missing.
cases.expected: Only ID 3 is returned. The observed-zero ID 1 is absent from the missingness result.
cases.verification: Assert[3] and separately assert that the zero-amount filter returns [1].

cases.title: Combine conditions with engine operators
cases.input_contract: Return ordered IDs with a known amount at least 10 and event_id less than 4. Combine parenthesized Column comparisons with engine Boolean operators in each language.
cases.expected: Only ID 2 qualifies. ID 4 fails the ID bound, ID 3 is missing, and ID 1 is below the amount threshold.
cases.verification: Assert the exact singleton and explain one exclusion reason for each other ID.

cases.title: Preserve NULL through a derived column
cases.input_contract: Return a DataFrame with event_id and amount_plus_one=amount_cents+1, without filling NULL or dropping identity. Keep a Long-compatible integer result.
cases.expected: Ordered rows are(1,1),(2,21),(3, NULL),(4,21). The two 21 values remain separate events and unknown remains unknown.
cases.verification: Compare every ordered row with literal expected values, including the NULL position.

cases.title: Compare SQL and Columns with an independent expectation
cases.input_contract: Register a session-local temporary view and return ordered IDs from SQL SELECT/WHERE amount_cents>10. Compare SQL and DataFrame paths to the literal expected IDs rather than only to one another.
cases.expected: Both paths return [2,4]. The temporary view exists only in this owned session and no external database connection is opened.
cases.verification: Assert SQL IDs and selectedIds against [2,4] independently, then let the complete program stop its session in finally.
